edge.title: Swap NS polar for Aurora; NorMuon-lite dropped; #12-based skeleton
edge.summary: Replaces the Newton–Schulz polar factor with Aurora's leverage-uniform polar on the non-square MLP matrices: a row-diagonal D (starting at inverse row norms, refined once with damping 0.5) is applied before NS so the orthogonal factor's row norms approach the uniform value √(n/m) = 0.5; square attention matrices still use plain NS. Contra-Muon (−0.2·ĝ) and the 0.35 u/w floor from #11 are kept, but NorMuon-lite's row/column variance normalization is gone and the script is built on #12's skeleton (Gaussian hidden init, zero biases, bf16 RMSNorm). The run is scheduled for 3200 steps and claimed at 3175.

changes.label: Polar step → Aurora (MLP matrices)
changes.detail: muon_update calls aurora_orthogonalize(pp_iterations=2, pp_beta=0.5): non-square G is transposed to tall, row-equilibrated by D, and polar(D·G) is returned with D refined once toward row norm² = n/m; square matrices fall back to zeropower_via_newtonschulz5.

changes.label: NorMuon-lite variance normalization
changes.detail: There is no second_moment state or per-row/column variance rescaling: the Aurora + Contra update goes from the aspect-ratio scale straight to the u/w floor (not mentioned in the README).

changes.label: Contra-Muon applied to Aurora output
changes.detail: Same CONTRA_MUON = 0.4 and 5-step power-iteration normalizer; 0.2·ĝ is subtracted from the Aurora polar factor and the result is rescaled to that factor's Frobenius norm.

changes.label: Init and RMSNorm taken from #12
changes.detail: Non-proj hidden weights are N(0, 0.33/fan_in) and all biases zero (vs PyTorch default uniform init in #11); RMSNorm uses F.rms_norm(x, weight=gains) in the activation dtype instead of an fp32 upcast.

changes.label: train_steps 3225 → 3200, claim 3175
changes.detail: Same linear cooldown (0.7); claimed at the 3175 checkpoint where the LR is ≈1.1% of peak. Muon weight_decay is passed as 0 (effective value unchanged from #11).

changes.label: #12 training-loop skeleton
changes.detail: num_trials loop, validation every 125 steps then every 25 in the last 10%, no NaN guard, no manual seed, no cuDNN-SDPA disable, docstrings.

edge.parent_check: Declared #11, but the code is #12's script plus Aurora and #11's Contra-Muon/u/w floor (nearest-code #12; the c17_p12 diff touches only the optimizer section, train_steps and the Muon constructor). From #11 it carries Contra-Muon (CONTRA_MUON = 0.4) and the u/w floor (TARGET_UW = 0.35) with lr 0.0375 and wd 0, but NOT NorMuon-lite; init, RMSNorm and the training loop are #12's.
edge.noise: Most of the textual diff vs #11 is #12's skeleton: inlined world_size/rank in the dataloader, num_trials loop, val cadence, removed seed/NaN-guard/cuDNN-SDPA lines, constants inlined, docstrings and comments.

techniques.note: Nesterov mu=0.95, 12 NS iters, √max(1, m/n) scale, lr 0.0375, wd 0; plain NS on square attn mats
MLP fc/proj: polar(D·G), row-diagonal D, pp_iterations=2, pp_beta=0.5, target row norm² n/m
0.2·M/σ̂max(M) subtracted from the Aurora polar factor (CONTRA_MUON=0.4), norm restored
update scaled up to ‖u‖_F/‖w‖_F = 0.35 when below (TARGET_UW); weight_decay=0
AdamW lr embed 0.3 / head 1/320 / 1-D 0.01, betas (0.8, 0.95), eps 1e-10, wd 0
flat, then linear to 0 over the last 70% of 3200 steps (all groups)
'proj' weights zeroed; all biases zero, other weights N(0, 0.33/fan_in) (#12-style)

hparams.hidden.optimizer: Muon with Aurora polar + Contra-Muon + u/w floor (no NorMuon-lite)
hparams.hidden.ns_iters: 12 (per NS call; Aurora makes 2 calls on MLP matrices)

mechanisms.name: Aurora leverage-uniform polar
mechanisms.explain: For a tall momentum matrix G (m > n; wide ones are transposed first), Aurora sets D = 1/‖G_i‖ per row, computes U = NS(D·G), then updates D ← D·((n/m)/‖U_i‖²)^0.5 and recomputes U = NS(D·G) (pp_iterations = 2). This equilibrates the row norms (leverage scores) of the orthogonal factor toward √(n/m) = 0.5, so no single fc output neuron or proj input column receives an outsized share of the update. Square attention matrices have no leverage freedom and use plain NS.

mechanisms.name: Mid-cooldown claim
mechanisms.explain: The linear schedule decays to 0 at train_steps = 3200, but the record is claimed at the fixed step-3175 checkpoint for all 20 seeds, where the LR is ≈1.1% of peak. Validation runs every 25 steps in the last 10% of training.

caveats: The README says the only algorithmic change vs #11 is polar(G) → polar(D·G), but the code also drops NorMuon-lite and changes init (zero biases, Gaussian hidden weights), so the Aurora effect is confounded with removing NorMuon-lite. The README's z = 0.886 / p = 0.188 omits the √n factor; the record qualifies via the precision criterion (3.28 − μ)·√20 = 0.00517 at step 3175. Aurora only changes the 24 non-square MLP matrices.
